title: Cryptographic hashing, HMAC, and secure random — directly in SQL
description: DuckDB ships with [`hash()`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/utility#hash) (non-cryptographic) and a built-in `sha256()`. The [Crypto extension](https://github.com/Query-farm/crypto) adds the full [SHA-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2) and [SHA-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-3) families, [BLAKE3](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3) and [BLAKE2b](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7693), [HMAC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2104), an order-deterministic aggregate hash, and a CSPRNG for keys, salts, and nonces. Scope is **hashing and authentication only** — no symmetric ciphers (AES), no password-hashing KDFs (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2), no public-key signing.

sections.title: What you get
sections.description: Four functions, organized around the primitives most data pipelines actually need from cryptography in SQL.

bulletPoints.label: Cryptographic hashes over any column
bulletPoints.description: [`crypto_hash`](#crypto_hash) over `VARCHAR`, `BLOB`, every numeric type, `BOOLEAN`, `DATE`, `TIME`, `TIMESTAMP`, `UUID`, and lists of fixed-length types. Algorithms: [BLAKE3](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3), `blake2b-512`, the full SHA-2 family (224/256/384/512), the full [SHA-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-3) family (224/256/384/512), Keccak (mapped to SHA-3), and the legacy MD4 / MD5 / SHA-1 for compatibility.

bulletPoints.label: Order-deterministic dataset checksum
bulletPoints.description: [`crypto_hash_agg`](#crypto_hash_agg) folds a column into one digest in `ORDER BY` order. By construction, `crypto_hash_agg('algo', col ORDER BY ord)` produces the same bytes as `crypto_hash('algo', LIST(col ORDER BY ord))` — so any client (Python, Go, Rust) that can build the equivalent ordered list can verify a DuckDB digest byte-for-byte.

bulletPoints.label: Keyed message authentication
bulletPoints.description: [`crypto_hmac`](#crypto_hmac) implements [HMAC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2104) with the same algorithm vocabulary as [`crypto_hash`](#crypto_hash) — for signing API requests, verifying webhook payloads, or per-row tamper detection. BLAKE3 keying requires a 32-byte key.

bulletPoints.label: Secure random bytes
bulletPoints.description: [`crypto_random_bytes`](#crypto_random_bytes) returns bytes from OpenSSL's [`RAND_bytes`](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man3/RAND_bytes.html) — the same CSPRNG TLS implementations rely on. Use for HMAC keys, salts, nonces, or random IDs.

sections.title: Type-aware, length-safe hashing
sections.description: The hashing surface is intentionally **type-sensitive** — `42::INTEGER` and `42::BIGINT` produce different digests because their binary representations differ. This is the right behaviour for cryptographic use: a hash that collapses across logically distinct domains is a footgun.

bulletPoints.label: Length-prefixed list elements
bulletPoints.description: Variable-length elements (`VARCHAR`, `BLOB`) inside a list are hashed as `[8-byte length][content]`. This defends against [length-extension-style ambiguity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_extension_attack) so that `['ab', 'c']` and `['a', 'bc']` produce distinct digests — both via [`crypto_hash`](#crypto_hash) on lists and via [`crypto_hash_agg`](#crypto_hash_agg) over `VARCHAR`/`BLOB` columns.

bulletPoints.label: Aggregate equals list
bulletPoints.description: `crypto_hash_agg('algo', col ORDER BY ord)` is byte-equal to `crypto_hash('algo', LIST(col ORDER BY ord))`. The `ORDER BY` is **mandatory** — DuckDB's [aggregate](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/aggregates) execution does not guarantee row order, so an unordered hash aggregate would be non-deterministic.

bulletPoints.label: NULL hashes to NULL
bulletPoints.description: [`crypto_hash`](#crypto_hash) and [`crypto_hmac`](#crypto_hmac) propagate NULL. [`crypto_hash_agg`](#crypto_hash_agg) returns NULL for empty groups. Treat NULL like any other column in your hash inputs — coalesce or cast it explicitly if you need a stable representation.

bulletPoints.label: BLOB output, hex it for display
bulletPoints.description: All three hash functions return [`BLOB`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/blob). Wrap with `lower(to_hex(...))` for a hex string, or compare BLOBs directly with `=` for byte-equality.

sections.title: Honest scope — what's not in this extension
sections.description: The extension is deliberately narrow. If your problem needs primitives from a wider library, you'll need to combine this with something else.

bulletPoints.label: No symmetric encryption
bulletPoints.description: There is no `crypto_encrypt` / `crypto_decrypt`. The extension does not implement AES (see [NIST FIPS 197](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.197.pdf)) or any other cipher. Encrypt-at-rest belongs at storage / file level, not in row expressions.

bulletPoints.label: No password-hashing KDFs
bulletPoints.description: No bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2, or PBKDF2. For storing user passwords, follow the [OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html) and run a real KDF in your application layer — DuckDB SQL is the wrong place for that work. Salts can be generated here with [`crypto_random_bytes`](#crypto_random_bytes); the actual KDF should not.

bulletPoints.label: No public-key signatures
bulletPoints.description: No RSA / ECDSA / Ed25519. Only symmetric authentication via [HMAC](#crypto_hmac).

bulletPoints.label: Legacy algorithms exposed for compatibility
bulletPoints.description: MD4, MD5, and SHA-1 are present so you can interop with existing systems, but they are **not cryptographically secure** for new designs. See [NIST SP 800-107 Rev. 1](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/107/r1/final) for current guidance — prefer [`sha2-256`](#crypto_hash), [`sha2-512`](#crypto_hash), or [`blake3`](#crypto_hash). MD4 may be disabled in modern OpenSSL builds.

useCases.title: Whole-dataset checksum / change detection
useCases.description: One [`crypto_hash_agg`](#crypto_hash_agg) over a sorted column produces a digest that any other system can recompute and compare. The fastest path from "did this partition change?" to a one-row answer.

useCases.title: Hash-chained audit trail
useCases.description: Combine [`crypto_hash`](#crypto_hash) with [`LAG`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/aggregates) over an ordered audit log to build a [Merkle-style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merkle_tree) hash chain. Tampering with any historical row breaks the chain at the first altered position. See the [hash-chain recipe](#cookbook).

useCases.title: Stable surrogate keys from many columns
useCases.description: Hash a tuple of source columns with [`crypto_hash`](#crypto_hash) to mint deterministic, idempotent IDs that survive re-runs. Useful for content-addressed storage and dedup pipelines.

useCases.title: API request signing and verification
useCases.description: [`crypto_hmac`](#crypto_hmac) with a shared secret signs outgoing payloads and verifies incoming ones, all in one SQL expression. Pair with [`crypto_random_bytes`](#crypto_random_bytes) for the secret itself.
